hero.label: How we build
hero.intro: Pagayo is a live SaaS platform — real tenants, real revenue, real production load. It is also a working example of what happens when you treat AI as development capacity inside a deliberate system, not as a shortcut around engineering.

workflow.label: How a change moves
workflow.headline: One path. No shortcuts.
workflow.intro: Every change — from a button colour to a schema migration — follows the same pipeline. Agents work inside it; they do not replace it.

founder.label: One founder. One platform.
founder.headline: Not a department. A system.
paragraphs: Pagayo is built by one founder — not a large engineering department, not an agency, not an offshore bench.
What makes that workable is not raw speed. It is architecture you can explain in one diagram, processes that survive a bad week, and quality systems that do not depend on memory or mood.

Most visitors do not ask whether AI helps. They ask how one person can operate a platform this broad — storefront, payments, edge cache, admin, marketing, migrations, staging, production — without the wheels coming off.
The operator is one person today. The playbooks, schemas, and review gates are version-controlled — they apply to whoever touches the code next, human or agent.

aiTeam.label: AI is not the tool. It is the team.
aiTeam.headline: Capacity, not magic.
paragraphs: At Pagayo, AI is development capacity: parallel workstreams, careful refactors, review passes, and research — staffed by different models with different strengths.

Documentation matters more than clever instructions. Context matters more than generation speed. Agents read the codebase, the schemas, the deploy playbooks, and the rules files first — not improvised chat prompts.
Models change. Tools change. The system that loads context, enforces boundaries, and ships through the same pipeline does not.

may: Create feature branches and open pull requests
Run tests, builds, and staging deploys via CI
Read logs and docs through scoped MCP tools
mayNot: Push to main or deploy to production
Skip review or bypass migration checks
Modify shared schema without a published package bump

operatingSystem.label: The operating system
operatingSystem.headline: A development system, not a pile of hacks.
operatingSystem.intro: Pagayo did not accumulate AI tricks. It accumulated structure — the kind that lets agents work safely at scale and lets a single operator stay in control.

pillars.title: Architecture
pillars.body: Multi-repo, edge-first, Order-First domain model. Clear boundaries so agents know where a change belongs — and where it does not.

pillars.title: Documentation
pillars.body: AGENTS.md, playbooks, interface matrices, design contracts. The platform teaches newcomers — human or agent — how to behave before they touch code.

pillars.title: Single source of truth
pillars.body: Schema, design tokens, pricing, config each live in one named home. Duplicated truth is where AI-assisted development quietly breaks.

pillars.title: AI governance
pillars.body: Deploy policy, branch rules, MCP boundaries, and explicit "may / may not" lists. Agents operate inside guardrails that are version-controlled and reviewable.
pillars.proofLabel: Pagayo on GitHub — PR checks & deploys →

pillars.title: Specialised agents
pillars.body: Backend, frontend, database review, security, testing, exploration — scoped roles instead of one generalist that guesses its way through everything.

pillars.title: Review processes
pillars.body: Pull requests, automated checks, AI review on diffs, founder sign-off on production. Speed without review is just faster drift.

pillars.title: Quality systems
pillars.body: Tests as documentation, migration checks, staging before production, structured errors. Quality is designed in — not hoped for after the fact.

lessons.label: What we learned
lessons.headline: Honest lessons from building this way.
lessons.intro: None of this arrived fully formed. These are the patterns that survived contact with production.

items.title: AI without architecture does not scale
items.body: It amplifies whatever mess already exists. Clear module boundaries and domain rules are prerequisites — not optional polish.

items.title: AI without documentation fails quietly
items.body: Agents guess. Humans patch. Drift compounds until nobody trusts the output. Written standards beat clever session prompts every time.

items.title: Prompts are not enough
items.body: Durable instructions live in version control: rules files, playbooks, schemas. Chat is for the task at hand — not for storing how the company builds software.

items.title: Governance grows with the system
items.body: What worked at three repositories breaks at twelve. Deploy policy, secret handling, and agent scope need to tighten as surface area grows — not loosen.

items.title: Quality comes from systems
items.body: Consistent patterns, automated checks, reviewable diffs, and staging validation beat hoping the model got lucky on the last turn.

longTerm.label: Built for the long term
longTerm.headline: Production, not a prototype.
paragraphs: Pagayo is not an experiment on a slide deck. It runs in production, serves live tenants, processes real payments, and ships improvements every week.
That constraint changes how you build. You cannot hand-wave migrations, skip tests, or "fix it in prod" when customers depend on the platform Monday morning.
The same systems that make AI-assisted development possible also make it responsible: staged deploys, observable errors, rollback paths, and a changelog you can point to.

helping.label: Helping others build differently
helping.headline: Occasionally, not as a business model.
paragraphs: We sometimes help software companies explore AI-native development practices — architecture, documentation, agent setup, governance — when the fit is right.
This is not a consultancy landing page. Pagayo remains the product. If you are building software and want to compare notes, we are open to a conversation.
